title: Wafer-scale thin-film PZT photonic integrated circuits enabling multi-terabit optical transmission - Nature Communications
byline: Zehao; Xie; Yujun; Wang; Jungan; Hang; Lin; Wei; Peng; Qiu; Feng; Zhao; Guangming; Ming
html:
Abstract

Meeting the escalating demand for high-capacity optical communication requires electro-optic (EO) photonic integrated circuits (PICs) that combine terabit-scale capacity, energy efficiency and scalable manufacturing. Here we establish thin-film lead zirconate titanate (PZT) as a wafer-scale photonic integration platform on 8-inch SiO2/Si substrates. Uniform, high-quality PZT thin films are prepared using a scalable chemical solution deposition–magnetron sputtering process, followed by a deep ultraviolet (DUV) stepper-based wafer-scale manufacturing process. Low propagation loss and low in-plane optical anisotropy provide the precise phase control and layout flexibility required for large-scale integration, supporting high-performance arrayed waveguide gratings (AWGs). Ferroelectric-domain engineering activates the strong Pockels response, enabling Mach–Zehnder modulators (MZMs) with a half-wave voltage–length product (VπL) of 1.19 V·cm, a broadband EO response extending to 70 GHz and data rates up to 224 Gbps. We further demonstrate a monolithically integrated 16-channel wavelength-division multiplexing transmitter supporting 3.2-Tbps-class optical interconnects. These results establish PZT as a practical wafer-scale platform for multi-terabit photonic systems.
